text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2% today as oil prices ticked up and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East kept crude supported. The U.S. oil benchmark closed around $89.50 per barrel, while reports of Iranian tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi refining capacity underscored ongoing supply-chain risks in a critical shipping chokepoint — the kind of disruption premium that typically lifts oil explorers and producers.

That said, the stock remains down 0.6% over the past two weeks, dragged down by last Sunday's climate summit collapse and a broader pullback in energy stocks. Reports suggest the refinery-trade boom that powered much of the energy sector's gains is unwinding, which may be tempering enthusiasm even as crude prices hold steady on geopolitical jitters.
